subject: Native metadata alignment for profile-neutral WVB 1.39
claim: The native metadata reader now matches the existing complete-verifier rule for WVB 1.39: present metadata sets a minimum profile, explicit broader hosted/system scope is preserved, and absent metadata remains supported. The retained metadata self-test passes 35 grouped checks on Windows and Debian with identical bytes. Full native WVB 1.39 admission remains closed.

source.value: Worktree based on c998c93b948b743cc5fbb3e2811328b30297a1d6; exact changed reader and self-test identities are recorded below.

limitations: Native-X64-Lowering-Core.wv still rejects minor 39 at its module-structure boundary. No borrowed native type representation, E1 lowering, lifetime/cleanup integration, native consumer migration, installed-tool promotion, or full native execution support is claimed.

This aligns an internal reader with Tools/Windvale.Verify/Wvb-Metadata-Normalization.wv; it does not define a new WVB metadata contract. Minor 39 permits a declared profile at least as broad as the metadata minimum, through profile 3. Versions 33 through 38 retain their system-profile rule; older versions retain exact derived-profile matching.

The initial uncommitted draft incorrectly required metadata presence for minor 39 and used exact profile equality. Review against the complete verifier caught that mismatch. The draft and its 32-group self-consistent test result were discarded before the final 35-group runs; they are not evidence for the committed behavior.

The added groups cover absent metadata, portable minimum under profiles 1/2/3, hosted minimum under profiles 2/3 with rejection at 1, system authority rejection below 3, unknown profiles, trailing bytes, every truncated prefix of a valid portable envelope, and oversized cursor/limit. The existing 19 groups remain in the same test.
The existing reconstruction owner already constructs and executes this self-test. Only that small project and its pinned runner were selected; no new verifier entry point was added.

The changed-file plan selected wvb-to-wvo-reconstruction and native-x64-lowering-development (360 expected seconds), plus editor verification. Full reconstruction, native machine emission, editor grammar, broad ABI/OS/bootstrap, and full qualification were not run: only a minor-39 metadata-reader branch and its fixture changed, while full minor-39 native admission remains closed and lexical rules are unchanged.

Run-Wvb executes the new test bytecode inside the pinned native bytecode interpreter. This is execution of the current metadata reader, not construction of a promoted native lowerer. Timings and peak working-set memory were not collected as a performance benchmark.

Consumer tracing found that Canonical-Package-Text.wv feeds Package-Lock.wv and Installation-Generation.wv; changing those maintained native paths to E1 borrowing before native support would break them. Native borrow representation, lowering, verification, ownership retention and cleanup must be integrated before that migration; no parallel parser or compatibility implementation was added.
